researched_by: user report from direct visit (Fontburn); not yet verified against published policy
policy_summary: Overnight parking is PERMITTED and CHARGED at Fontburn, GBP10, with payment deferrable to the next day where the machine is off and there is no signal. This is provision with a permissive posture - a materially different stance from the councils researched so far, and the far end of the spectrum from Cornwall's GBP70 PCN for leaving a motorhome overnight. Unknown whether this is a Fontburn arrangement or a Northumbrian Water tariff across Derwent, Kielder and other sites. That distinction decides whether water companies are a per-site job or a per-company one.
open_questions: Is the £10 signed at the car park, or published online only? Decides scrapeability.
Any conditions - self-containment, max nights, arrival/departure times, awnings?
Does the same apply at Derwent and Kielder Water?

sites.name: Fontburn Reservoir
sites.payment_notes: Machine is not always on. Hut only when staffed. Online otherwise - and if there is no signal, payment can be settled the next day.
sites.notes: Reported by a regular visitor, so price, payment routes and the next-day grace are reliable. Conditions and hours still unknown. The deferred-payment arrangement matters: it means no signal does not prevent staying, which is the opposite of how a strict enforcement regime would handle it.
